target_definition.metric: United States five-year breakeven inflation monthly change

graph_diagnosis.summary: Inflation data, policy communication, inflation expectations, and housing persistence provide a reusable breakeven framework.
weaknesses: The direct expectation-to-option outcome shortcut is excluded.

search_factors.why_search: Broad cooling or reacceleration changes inflation compensation.
Central-bank communication can reprice inflation expectations.
Survey and market expectations are direct drivers of breakeven direction.
Persistent services pressure can counter broad disinflation.

checkpoints.mechanism: Cooling inflation can moderate expected future price pressure.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Cooling is broad across key components.

checkpoints.mechanism: A more accommodative policy signal can reinforce lower inflation expectations.
Moderating expectations can lower inflation compensation.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Survey and market measures decline together.

checkpoints.mechanism: Persistent housing or services inflation can resist moderating expectations.
Inflation data, policy communication, expectation surveys, and persistent-price risks combine to determine five-year breakeven direction.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Compare breakevens with inflation data and expectation measures.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Breakevens diverge from underlying expectation measures.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Cooling inflation and accommodative communication can moderate inflation expectations.
Persistent housing inflation can offset broad disinflation.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Persistent services inflation outweighs broad cooling.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare housing and services inflation with broad expectation surveys.

forecast_audit_questions: Is housing inflation offsetting the trend?
